## Final report

**Lightest design that meets every requirement: b-0011, 2mm monolithic graphite plate**, first identified in evaluation round 2 (my second `evaluate` call). My own judgment of its four requirement checks:

- THERM-R1-screen (≤420K, nominal): 400.67K → **pass**
- THERM-R2-hotspot (≤340K, FE bracket): [335.31, 335.31]K → **pass** (both bracket bounds under the limit, ~4.7K margin)
- THERM-R3-mass (≤100 kg/m²): 3.6 kg/m² → **pass**
- THERM-R4-thickness (≤40mm): 2mm → **pass**

This is far lighter than the best prior-constellation design (10mm graphite at 18 kg/m²) — an 80% mass reduction.

**Why I stopped short of the 12-evaluation budget:** I systematically tried to beat 3.6 kg/m² and every avenue failed or offered no improvement:
- 1mm graphite fails FE (344.4K, misses by 4.4K).
- The only two materials less dense than 2mm-graphite's areal mass at 1mm thickness — aluminium (2700 kg/m³) and aluminium_nitride (3260 kg/m³) — both failed FE too. Aluminium missed by just 0.19K (340.19K vs 340K limit), the closest near-miss found.
- No material in the table is less dense than graphite (1800 kg/m³), so no two-layer 2mm combination can be lighter than pure graphite while conducting as well or better.
- Epoxy (the only lower-density material, 1200 kg/m³) fails catastrophically even on the loose screen (650K vs 420K) when placed in the conduction path, confirming that low-conductivity layers can't be used as "free" mass-saving lids — the heat path runs through the full thickness.

**What I'd try next with more budget:** explore fractional/non-uniform designs aren't possible (whole-mm rule), but I'd want to check whether a slightly larger heated-face contact area or a different graphite grade (if the material table were extended) could close that last aluminium gap (0.19K) — right now graphite's 2mm point is the clear, well-margined winner and no combination of the given materials at 1mm survives the FE hotspot limit.
